name: Number of distinct residues of all factorials mod prime(n).
comment: The standard (folklore?) conjecture is that a(n)/prime(n) = 1 - 1/e = 0.63212.... - _Charles R Greathouse IV_, May 11 2015
link: Amiram Eldar, Table of n, a(n) for n = 1..10000 (terms 1...1000 from Alois P. Heinz)
Yong-Gao Chen and Li-Xia Dai, Congruences with factorials modulo p, INTEGERS 6 (2006), #A21.
example: Let n=4, p_4=7. We have modulo 7: 1!==1, 2!==2, 3!==6, 4!==3, 5!==1, 6!==6 and for m>=7, m!==0, such that we have 5 distinct residues 0,1,2,3,6. Therefore a(4) = 5.
maple: a:= proc(n) local p, m, i, s;
for i to p do m:= m*i mod p; s:=s union {m} od;
program: (PARI) apply(p->#Set(vector(p,n,n!)%p), primes(100)) \\ _Charles R Greathouse IV_, May 11 2015
